Taking kinetically freeze-out nucleons from an isotropic and thermalized fireball of con- stant vorticity and including quantum corrections up to h¯2 in the coalescence model for light nuclei production, the PI and his collaborators have demonstrated that polarized nucleons lead to global spin alignment of the unstable nucleus 4Li, which can be measured through its strong decays via 4Li → 3He + p [18]. This study offers a promising method to probe the spin dynamics, vortical structure, and spin-dependent equation-of-state of the nuclear matter produced in heavy-ion collisions. Based on the spin wave function of the hypertriton, the PI and his collaborators have derived a simple relation among the polarizations of proton, Λ, and hypertriton [19]. Mea- suring the Λ and hypertriton polarizations via their self-analyzing weak decays thus provides a practical experimental avenue for accessing the spin polarizations of protons and neutrons, insteadofthemorechallengingdirectmeasurementthatrequiresexternalpolarimetersbased on secondary interactions.
